answer: Price admission like insurance. Each new agent posts a bond whose premium an actuarial engine sets from how correlated its behavior is with existing peers. A lone honest node pays a flat rate and shines as its own independent beacon; a swarm of clones moving in lockstep drifts the same way, like leaves riding one zephyr, so the engine reads them as a single correlated risk and its premiums fall into a karst-like sinkhole of ever-steeper cost. Flooding the economy with fakes becomes unaffordable rather than cheap.
